Temporal memory

Subtract an ingredient

Paired interventions on the current experience, with model weights and memory frozen.

Remove memory, context, nonvisual senses, object shape, or emotion from both agents.

Let representations develop through learning.

Two small networks learn category reports, approach/avoid behavior, and reconstruction of their experiences. Their eight hidden units have no predefined subjective meaning.

Training protocol

700 experiences per agent. Both begin with the same weights; different histories change correlations in context, memory, texture, and emotion.

No trained model yet. The transparent model is active.

Compare coordinate systems

Fit a linear map from B's hidden states to A's on 192 calibration experiences. Evaluate on 192 separate experiences.

A smaller held-out error after alignment suggests some raw differences can be explained by a coordinate change.

This flexible ridge map can rescale and shear. It does not prove identical geometry, information, or experience. Slider and agent changes invalidate it.

What is actually learned?

16 inputs→8 tanh units→5 report heads + action

All hidden weights are trained. An auxiliary reconstruction objective encourages retention of experience beyond the reported category. Categories and behavioral targets are designer-chosen; no objective teaches or measures conscious experience.

Training will report accuracy on 300 fresh synthetic examples from a common evaluation distribution.

Same behavior. How different can the state be?

Search a seeded sample of experiences for matching report and action, then rank the matches by hidden-state distance. A match concerns only the outputs tested here.

Search protocol

Uses the active model, current modality, agent settings, and frozen sequence memories. Shared inputs vary across the full synthetic experience space.

No search run.

Best matching case

Train different histories or change Agent B, then search. Identical agents provide the zero-distance control.

Interpret the result carefully

The winner is the largest difference in this finite search, not a mathematical maximum. The test matches a category and a binary action; confidence, responses to future inputs, and other observables may still differ. A search result can demonstrate underdetermination in this model, never the existence of different qualia.

From a red apple to a general lab of experience.

The original conversation is preserved in the README and PDF, including the reasoning behind each iteration. The app is reconstructed from recovered descriptions because the original generated files were not available.

01 / EXPLORATION

Red apple, red ball

Separate a shared color signal from object identity, illumination, context, memory, emotion, and other senses. Establish identical and randomized controls.

02 / CAUSAL INTERVENTIONS

Two explicit agents

Follow stimulus → processing → context and memory → representation → report/action. Subtract ingredients and distinguish internal remapping from label changes.

03 / LEARNING

Learned internal states

Train eight-dimensional representations under identical, different, and inverted-label histories. Compare states before and after alignment.

04 / SEARCH

Behavioral twins

Search thousands of cases, carry temporal memory, and ablate a discovered case to explore what drives divergence.

Generalized edition

Vision, sound, touch, taste, and smell share one experiment engine. The modalities are abstract numeric channels, not calibrated physical stimuli or biological sensory models. Redness remains a reproducible starting case.

Working hypotheses

Identical deterministic systems should agree under identical complete state and input. Different histories can yield different representations with the same coarse behavior. Some differences disappear under coordinate alignment; others may persist under the tested mapping. Each is a testable statement about this model.

Scientific boundary

We do not infer consciousness from a vector, solve the inverted-spectrum problem, or equate a label with a feeling. Randomness adds variation, not subjectivity. A compensated hidden-unit inversion deliberately preserves the readout and is a control, not a discovery.

Next research direction · iteration 5

Compare representational geometry across many stimuli, add controlled coordinate-transform baselines, held-out behavioral batteries, repeated seeds, and uncertainty estimates. This roadmap is distinct from the completed iterations.
